title: Eggs: protein, fat, calories, and key nutrients

seo.title: Egg nutrition: protein, fat, calories, choline, B12
seo.meta_description: One large egg provides about 70–80 calories, 6–6.5 g protein and about 5 g fat. It also supplies choline, B12, selenium and other nutrients.
seo.search_intent: Understand whole-egg nutrition per 100 g and per large egg, including protein, fat, calories, choline and micronutrients.

excerpt: A large egg does not contain 10 or 12 grams of protein; it is closer to 6–6.5 grams. It provides roughly 70–80 calories and about 5 grams fat, mostly in the yolk, plus choline, vitamin B12, selenium and other micronutrients.
content_html:
Eggs pack a substantial amount of nutrition into a small portion. One large egg, roughly 50 g edible weight, provides about 6–6.5 g protein, around 5 g fat, and roughly 70–80 calories. The final number changes with egg size and added cooking fat.

Per 100 g and per large egg

Nutrient100 g hard-boiled egg1 large egg (~50 g)
Calories~155~78
Protein~12.6 g~6.3 g
Fat~10.6 g~5.3 g
Saturated fat~3.3 g~1.6 g
Carbohydrate~1.1 g~0.6 g

Those values describe whole cooked egg without added oil. A fried egg can contain more energy if it retains butter or oil from the pan.

Protein comes from both the white and the yolk

Egg white is mostly water and protein with almost no fat. The yolk contains nearly all the fat and many of the vitamins and minerals, but it also contains protein. Removing every yolk lowers calories and fat but also removes a substantial share of the egg’s micronutrients.

Eggs are particularly rich in choline

NIH lists about 147 mg choline in one large hard-boiled egg. Adult Adequate Intakes are 550 mg/day for men and 425 mg/day for women, so one egg provides roughly 27% and 35% of those amounts, respectively.

Choline is involved in cell membranes, neurotransmission, lipid transport, and other functions.

They also provide B12, selenium, and vitamin D

NIH food tables list about 0.5 mcg vitamin B12 per cooked egg. USDA’s hard-boiled entry provides roughly 2.2 mcg vitamin D per 100 g along with meaningful selenium, phosphorus, and riboflavin.

Eggs are not a fiber food—they contain 0 g—and their calcium content is modest compared with dairy or bone-in canned fish.

What about cholesterol?

Dietary cholesterol is concentrated in the yolk. A hard-boiled USDA reference is about 373 mg/100 g, or roughly 185–190 mg in a 50 g egg. Dietary cholesterol is not the same measurement as blood cholesterol, and the response to it depends on the overall diet and individual physiology.

Cooking method mostly changes what you add

Boiling and poaching require no added fat. Ten grams of oil contains about 90 calories, so a fried egg’s calorie total depends partly on how much cooking fat actually remains with the food.

The useful takeaway

A large egg provides about 6.3 g protein and roughly 78 calories; it is not an enormous isolated protein dose. Its value is the combination of high-quality protein with fat, choline, B12, selenium, and other micronutrients in a compact serving.

faq.question: How much protein is in one egg?
faq.answer: A large egg, about 50 g edible weight, provides roughly 6–6.5 g protein.

faq.question: How many calories are in a large egg?
faq.answer: A large cooked egg without added fat is roughly 75–80 calories.

faq.question: What nutrient are eggs especially high in?
faq.answer: Choline stands out: NIH lists about 147 mg in one large hard-boiled egg, along with B12, selenium and other nutrients.
